html:
Ahmad Yasawi (1093 to 1166) was a Sufi teacher and poet in the town of Yasi, now Turkistan in southern Kazakhstan. He founded the Yasawiyya, the first Sufi order of the Turkic world, and he is the earliest known poet to write in Turkic.

Born in Sayram, he studied in Bukhara under the Persian Sufi Yusuf Hamadani. He taught in simple verse, in a language herders could understand, and his poems were later gathered as the Diwan-i Hikmet, the "Book of Wisdom", though much of it was written down long after his death. His dervishes carried Islam to the nomads of the Kipchak steppe and on into Anatolia, and later orders such as the Naqshbandiyya and the Bektashis traced links to him.

Tradition says that at 63, the age at which the Prophet died, he withdrew to an underground cell for the rest of his life. Two centuries later Timur raised the great mausoleum over his grave, which became the main pilgrimage site of the steppe. His memory is central to the Islam of the Kazakhs and other Turkic peoples.
